plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Bare branches are covered in fragrant blossoms before any leaves appear. The flowers are spicy-sweet and open while the days are still cold. In Japan's plum groves they are a hopeful sign that spring is near.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter, roughly January to March, with peak bloom in February
plants.location: Japan, with ume groves and gardens across Honshu
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry blossoms. In East Asian art it is a symbol of perseverance because it flowers through the cold.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, bell-shaped white flowers with small green marks on the inner petals push up through frosty soil, sometimes through snow. They carpet woodlands, hedge banks and churchyards in drifts of white.
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens across Britain and temperate Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make a natural antifreeze-like protein that helps them cope with cold. The bulbs also contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medicine.

plants.name: Agapanthus africanus
plants.description: Rounded clusters of tubular, deep blue flowers rise on slender stems above arching, strap-like leaves. They add a late-summer splash of color to gardens and rocky slopes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly December to February, with some flowers into March
plants.location: Western Cape, South Africa, where it is native, and in gardens across the southern hemisphere
plants.funFact: Its name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'. Despite the common name 'African lily', it is not a true lily.
